correctness.rationale: The line graph has a 2r-clique of spokes and one degree-two rim vertex per page. For metric resolution, every page needs a spoke and at most one page can contribute only one landmark; the equality family is then proved resolving by explicit omitted-edge comparisons. For double resolution, any page with fewer than two selected edges either leaves its spokes unresolved or gives a constant -1 distance-difference vector for a spoke-rim pair. Any two-per-page set is doubly resolving by explicit selected/omitted pair cases. The direct checker exhaustively confirms all smaller sets and all minimum sets for r=2..6.

value.rationale: Friendship graphs are a standard wheel-related benchmark family. The result simultaneously determines both edge-landmark resolution parameters, completely classifies and counts all minimum sets, and exhibits a uniform sharp gap of one between the two notions emphasized by the defining literature. This is a structural infinite-family theorem rather than a routine finite computation or a renamed standard edge-metric result.
